posts.name: byc
posts.cooked:
phantaskippy:

I've probably been the most critical of Nightmist of anyone, she really isn't for me, but she doesn't need fixing.Fixer's strengths are far more subtle than other heroes, it takes a while to really appreciate what he can bring to a team.

I've been playing as Fixer a lot lately, and he's really really versatile when it comes to damage dealing and damage redirection.  His main issue is heavy heavy reliance on damage boosting via equipments and ongoings, so when a villain clears the board, it takes him 2 turns to get back up and running.

I haven't really read any of the "fix Fixer" type threads, but I feel his weakness is he's only a damage dealer/redirector, and that other heroes do that better than he does in different ways.

Example, Harmony, Alternating Tiger Style, and Jack Handle hurts all non-heroes and ignores damage reduction.  But it's only 2 damage to all non-heroes that needed 3 cards to setup.  Expat can do that with Submachine Gun + Incendiary/Hollow Points, even if she can't get pass DR.  Ra can hit almost everybody with any of his +1 damage and Inferno.  AZ can dish out tons of damage and heal himself with both modules + Thermal Shockwave.

I feel that with all of the setup Fixer needs, the result is good, not great.  AZ with his setup = great.  Bunker with his setup = great.  Nightmist with setup = great.  Fixer is more flexible with his damage dealing/redirection in the sense that he can still be effective (just Dual Crowbars, thats fine, just Driving Mantis, cool).  But once he does get his setup (example, Grease Monkey, Dual Crowbars, Harmony is his best outright damage dealing setup probably), the results aren't as great as others are.  For 3+ card setups, I would want a better output.  I know that was probably by design because he seems to be flexibility vs. output, but it's hard to watch it in action when things are going the heroes way, and he seems to lag behind.

Fixer certainly loves when others are boosting his damage, then he gets ridiculous.

I am most frustated by Fixer when I can't get the style and/or tool I need right at that time.  His design really requires for him to get that style/tool out, and when it doesn't happen, he feels like a terrible character.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Fixer isn't just about damage, though - don't forget stuff like Grease Gun and Salvage Yard for nerfing the bad guys and recovering from equipment wipes, respectively.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Salvage Yard is one of the single best cards in the game.

Everyone recovers all equipment in their trash, to their hand.  No other card recovers cards from the trash nearly as effectively.  It may not be good for equp low heroes on your team, but it is wicked for Omnitron-X, Expatriette, and Bunker.

I've said it before with Expat, if you have a Fixer and get speed loading it is amazing, cause Fixer can pull them all back out for you, and with Bunker you can discard equips for gatling or explode them with Omni and Fixer pulls them right back out (even through no draw) and lets you do it again.

With Omni he's a super quick recovery from a component wipe or a self-destruct/Singularity.  AZ, Wraith and Chrono he saves from destruction, although they need it less.

And if you have an overdrive in the trash and you get to play it out of turn, it is epic.

You also have to add in Charge, it gives you a second attack that is one better than your normal attack.

Hoist Chain and Tiger is an epic combo, Just cause an enemy has DR doesn't mean you can't reduce their damage dealt.  I've crushed Voss' flip side damage with a Charge and strike, even though there were two gaurds out, Tire Iron Tiger is also great, since you can one-shot a 3hp minion that is hiding behind reduction.

Add in the always awesome Bloody Knuckles on a turn where Adept is going to let you overdrive and you really can get some good damage out of Fixer, it is just a secondary thing for him, his versatility is his main strength.

Grease gun is also a great card, and the fact that you can put it back in hand with salvage yard is sweet.  It is again even better with an out of turn card play, so you don't skip your turn.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
byc:

I haven't really read any of the "fix Fixer" type threads, but I feel his weakness is he's only a damage dealer/redirector

Personally I'm extremely sad that Bloody Knuckles turns off his Driving Mantis style (which is the only one of the Styles I really like, though Grease Monkey Fist is obviously more directly useful, and Alternating Tiger Claw is a potential magic bullet…I still maintain that Riveting Crane is more often than not useless).  But my main frustration with him is that I always seem to draw more Styles than Tools (I don't know if that's just bad luck or if styles are actually thicker in his deck, although he definitely only has a tutor for Styles, when he really needs one for Tools).  If you can get a Tool you're golden, but if not, you end up with multiple styles and no ability to switch without squandering your irreplaceable cards.  He definitely does not have the perfect flow of a zen master; the intention might have been to make him feel gritty by trying to force you to make hard decisions, but if so, the payoff is much too low, and I just end up wanting to have him draw two cards on turn 1 the next time I play him, since it's better for him to dig into his deck than make suboptimal plays and then plink for 1 with an unimproved Strike.

Example, Harmony, Alternating Tiger Style, and Jack Handle hurts all non-heroes and ignores damage reduction.  But it's only 2 damage to all non-heroes that needed 3 cards to setup.  Expat can do that with Submachine Gun + Incendiary/Hollow Points, even if she can't get pass DR.

Unless Expat has four cards (a second Ammo of similar quality plus Speed Loading), she only gets that megablast once.  Fixer with the proper combo can do it every turn, so they're hardly equivalent.  That said, I've found Expat to be much more consistently effective.

I feel that with all of the setup Fixer needs, the result is good, not great.

+1.  Though I also feel the Argent Adeopt often deserves this.  His results are more impressive, but not necessarily more useful, unless he gets a really lucky draw (either directly or through Arcane Cadence, which also requires luck).

posts.name: dragon2439
posts.cooked:
Nightmist is my favorite hero by far. Her versatility, controlled chaos and using her health as one of her resources make her a blast to play. Every turn I feel like a have a few options and get to weigh risk vs reward vs need. Granted everyone does that, but with her it feels so dynamic and fluid. I also love her thematically. That mythos combined with drawing power from doing a little damage to yourself and unleashing fury on everything is awesome.

Tempest would be my second hero. While his turns dont have the same decision making to risk vs reward vs need, I do like characters that can do anything. He can damage, clear the field, bounce terrible cards, send the environment packing, and help his team recover cards and even health. Cleansing downpour is my favorite card in his deck, and i've won us a few games simply by keeping everyone alive longer then we thought would be possible.
